questions.questionText: The soup was so ___ that the child refused to ___ it.
questions.explanation: A child refuses food that tastes bitter; 'swallow' completes the idea.

questions.questionText: The students were ___ when the teacher announced that the test was ___.
questions.explanation: Cancellation of a test pleases students; the other pairs are illogical.

questions.questionText: ___ it was raining heavily, the match ___ on time.
questions.explanation: Contrast between rain and starting on time needs 'Although'.

questions.questionText: The more you practise, the ___ you become and the ___ mistakes you make.
questions.explanation: Comparative 'better'; 'fewer' with countable 'mistakes'.

questions.questionText: She topped the class because she is ___ intelligent ___ hardworking.
questions.explanation: Topping the class needs positive qualities joined by 'both ... and'.

questions.questionText: ___ Ravi ___ his brother has passed the exam; both failed.
questions.explanation: 'Both failed' means neither passed: 'Neither ... nor'.

questions.questionText: By the time I ___ home, the match ___ already begun.
questions.explanation: Past event with an earlier past action takes simple past + past perfect (had begun).

questions.questionText: If he ___ harder, he ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the hotel's food was so ___ that guests kept returning.
questions.explanation: Guests return when food quality is excellent.

questions.questionText: She is taller ___ her sister but not as fair ___ her.
questions.explanation: Comparative 'taller' takes 'than'; 'not as fair' takes 'as'.

questions.questionText: Please ___ me your pen; I will ___ it back tomorrow.
questions.explanation: You lend something to someone; the borrower returns it.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the movie was so ___ that people left halfway.
questions.explanation: People leave a movie when the plot is dull.

questions.questionText: The patient was ___ to hospital after he ___ unconscious.
questions.explanation: Past passive 'was rushed' and past 'fell' (sequence of past events).

questions.questionText: Not only ___ he win the race, ___ he broke the record.
questions.explanation: 'Not only did he ..., but ...' is the correct inversion pattern.

questions.questionText: Unless you ___ hard, you will ___ the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative; the result of not working is failing.

questions.questionText: The accused was ___ because the evidence was too ___ to convict him.
questions.explanation: Weak evidence cannot convict, so he was acquitted.

questions.questionText: Of the two candidates Arun is the ___ qualified, but among all the staff Meera is the ___ qualified.
questions.explanation: Two items: comparative 'more'; many items: superlative 'most'.

questions.questionText: He ___ to the doctor, but the doctor ___ already left.
questions.explanation: Earlier past action (left) takes past perfect 'had'.

questions.questionText: Because the road was ___, the bus ___ slowly.
questions.explanation: Adjective 'slippery' describes the road; past tense 'moved'.

questions.questionText: The harder she studies, the ___ marks she ___.
questions.explanation: 'The + comparative' pattern; singular subject takes 'scores'.

questions.questionText: My uncle, ___ lives in Pune, ___ a retired engineer.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject for a person; singular subject takes 'is'.

questions.questionText: The book ___ I bought yesterday ___ very interesting.
questions.explanation: 'Which' for things; 'book' is singular so 'is'.

questions.questionText: He ___ for the bus for an hour when it finally ___.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous for the earlier ongoing action; simple past for the later event.

questions.questionText: The river ___ its banks and ___ the villages.
questions.explanation: Past of overflow is 'overflowed'; the water 'flooded' the villages.

questions.questionText: Neither the captain ___ the players ___ ready for the final.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor'; the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players' (were).

questions.questionText: A number of students ___ absent, but the number of absentees ___ small.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes plural; 'the number of' takes singular.

questions.questionText: I would have called you if I ___ your number, but I ___ it.
questions.explanation: Third conditional needs 'had known'; the real fact is past: 'did not know'.

questions.questionText: He is ___ MBA and his brother is ___ engineer.
questions.explanation: Article depends on sound: 'MBA' begins with the vowel sound 'em', and 'engineer' with a vowel.

questions.questionText: She is senior ___ me ___ three years.
questions.explanation: 'Senior' takes 'to'; the difference is shown with 'by'.

questions.questionText: He prefers tea ___ coffee, ___ his sister prefers coffee to tea.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to'; the two preferences contrast, so 'but'.

questions.questionText: She has ___ been to Goa, so she is ___ excited about the trip.
questions.explanation: 'Never' fits the 'so' clause of excitement; 'ever' is not used in a positive statement; 'very' goes with adjectives.

questions.questionText: Hardly ___ he sat down ___ the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly had ... when' is the fixed pattern ('than' goes with 'no sooner').

questions.questionText: She ___ me yesterday that she ___ come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Told' takes an object; the reported past needs 'would'.

questions.questionText: The principal, as well as the teachers, ___ pleased, and the students ___ also happy.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' does not change the subject (principal: was); 'students' takes 'were'.

questions.questionText: Had I ___ about the strike, I ___ left home earlier.
questions.explanation: Inverted third conditional: 'Had + past participle ..., would have + past participle'.

questions.questionText: Of the two proposals, the second is the ___ and it is also ___ practical.
questions.explanation: Two items need comparatives: better, more.

questions.questionText: She speaks as if she ___ the manager, though she ___ only a clerk.
questions.explanation: 'As if' for an unreal comparison takes 'were'; the fact is stated in present 'is'.

questions.questionText: The scheme, ___ aims at rural employment, ___ launched in 2006.
questions.explanation: 'Which' refers to the scheme (thing); singular 'was'.

questions.questionText: The flowers ___ I received were so ___ that the entire room smelt wonderful.
questions.explanation: 'Which' for things; smelling wonderful requires the adjective 'fragrant'.

questions.questionText: Seldom ___ he lose his temper, and rarely ___ he complain.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbs at the start take auxiliary inversion; singular 'he' takes 'does'.

questions.questionText: Each of the boys ___ his own bag, and all of them ___ ready to leave.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular (has); 'all of them' is plural (are).

questions.questionText: Rohan is not ___ clever ___ his sister, but he works harder.
questions.explanation: Negative equality uses 'as ... as'; 'than' never follows 'as'.
